one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-23 to 2026-11-22. No AT&T earnings (next late Jan 2027) and no ex-dividend (last 2026-10-09, next ~Jan 2027). Scheduled: Verizon 3Q26 on 2026-10-26 and T-Mobile 3Q26 in late October (read-across on promotions and postpaid adds), the FCC open meeting vote on the Supplemental Coverage from Space rules on 2026-10-29 (carriers asked to strip 2.5/3.45 GHz and keep consent; an adverse vote is a modest negative), and unscheduled SpaceX headlines (tower-lease signing with Crown Castle or others, spectrum closing) that drove the Oct-9 and Oct-23 drops. The stock fell 16% in 11 sessions on sector news rather than its own earnings path, which historically favours partial reversal, but the headline risk is skewed down. I centre the month at ~$21.0 (slight reversal drift, +0.4%) with ~9.5% monthly vol (above the 30%/3.5 = 8.6% base given recent 6-10% daily moves) plus a 15% weight fat-tail component for another SpaceX shock.

bear.story: SpaceX signs leases on ~80,000 towers and the spectrum deal closes in H1 2027; Starlink Mobile targets price-sensitive users (TD Cowen: AT&T base most willing to try it), VZ/TMUS answer with promotions, AT&T wireless ARPU falls ~3% below path and the market prices a 4-player US market (EV/EBITDA ~5.2x, P/E ~7x).

bull.story: Tower talks stall or turn into a wholesale/partner deal, the FCC keeps carrier consent on satellite use, AT&T keeps 4% ARPU growth on pricing and converged fiber, and the stock re-rates toward 7.0x EBITDA / 8.8x P/E.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Only 8 listed US comparables with relevant mixes exist (the US market has three national wireless carriers and two large cable operators); TMUS and VZ are the true peers, cable and small fiber names bracket the broadband side. The P/E above the median is driven by the cable names' structural broadband share losses (CHTR 2.5x reflects equity leverage and subscriber declines): AT&T's EPS compounds ~10%/yr to 2028 (guide and build) vs VZ +5% and CMCSA +3%, with 43% converged fiber+wireless households. I set it below VZ's 8.7x because AT&T's base is the most willing to try Starlink Mobile (TD Cowen 52% vs Verizon 23%) and leverage rose to 3.13x.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$16.50 (bear value $16.0) the stock would price ~5.3x NTM EBITDA / ~5.7x EPS, i.e. a structural loss of wireless pricing power: that would most likely mean SpaceX has signed tower access and a launch date, a price war has started (ARPU turning negative), or the $24B buyback / $1.11 dividend plan is being cut to defend the 2.5x leverage target. Ordinary 30% volatility alone puts the 1-sigma low near $15.5 only with a fundamental trigger.

reasoning: Facts: FY2025 revenue $125.6B, adj. EBITDA $46.4B, adj. EPS $2.12; 3Q26 adj. EPS $0.65 (GAAP $0.12-0.13 after a $2.6B Mexico impairment and ~$0.8B separation charges), FY26 guide raised to ~$2.40; net debt $149.8B (3.13x) after the $22.65B EchoStar spectrum; Mexico and Forged Fiber held for sale. Price moves: Oct-9 -10.8% = SpaceX agreeing to buy nationwide low-band spectrum for Starlink Mobile plus the $0.2775 ex-dividend (~1.1pt): multiple only. Oct-21 -6.4% = results day: adds slowed to 379K, fiber ARPU -4% with Q4 guided similar, Q4 EBITDA headwinds, leverage target pushed to 2029: a small change to the earnings path that I carry in the fiber ARPU driver. Oct-23 -8.0% = Bloomberg report SpaceX seeks >=80,000 US cell sites (TMUS also -8%, tower owners up): multiple only. Alternative-lane evidence: Polymarket prices 13% (mid-2027) and 34.5% (end-2027) that SpaceX becomes a US carrier (thin, ~$15k volume each); SpaceX's Starlink Mobile postings are mostly satellite D2D RAN roles; TD Cowen's survey says AT&T customers are the most willing to try Starlink Mobile (52% vs Verizon 23%), though only 34% overall would consider switching and price is the main lure (PhoneArena poll ~60%); AT&T's price hikes (legacy plans +$5-10, fee +$1) are visible in the 4% ARPU growth; network data (Opensignal/Ookla) put AT&T first on time-on-network and fastest-improving, not a churn trigger. Model: six drivers (postpaid phone subs, wireless ARPU, fiber+AIA connections, home internet ARPU, Legacy retention, capital investment) computing 86% of revenue; EBITDA grows below the company plan, EPS lands on the guide thanks to buybacks. Research target (12m) $23.09 from EV/EBITDA 6.2x, P/E 8.0x and a 12% FCF yield, all at or below today's de-rated levels; no custom leg; the stated EPS and FCF/share are not driver-linked. Ladder: mixture of the engine's scenarios (bear $16.0 25%, base $23.1 50%, bull $28.4 25%, 15%/13% within-scenario vol) blended 75/25 with a 30%-vol random walk around $20.93 (+3% drift) to respect momentum and base rates; median ~$22.6, P(>=21) 61%.

bear.story: SpaceX signs leases on ~80,000 towers and the spectrum deal closes in H1 2027; Starlink Mobile targets price-sensitive users (TD Cowen: AT&T base most willing to try it), VZ/TMUS answer with promotions, AT&T wireless ARPU falls ~3% below path and the market prices a 4-player US market (EV/EBITDA ~5.2x, P/E ~7x).

base.story: Build as set: ~1.0M/0.7M postpaid phone adds, ARPU +2%/+1%, ~2.3M/2.0M fiber+AIA adds, Legacy -27%/-30%, capex $22.5B; SpaceX overhang persists without a launch (Polymarket 13% by mid-2027) and the multiple stays near today's de-rated 6.2x/8.0x.

bull.story: Tower talks stall or turn into a wholesale/partner deal, the FCC keeps carrier consent on satellite use, AT&T keeps 4% ARPU growth on pricing and converged fiber, and the stock re-rates toward 7.0x EBITDA / 8.8x P/E.

model_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led telecom build (no DCF; policy). Five segments: AC Wireless and Home (driven: postpaid phone subs x wireless service revenue per sub + subs x FY2025 equipment revenue per sub $310.6/yr + consumer fiber/AIA connections x ARPU), AC Business Wireline (business fiber, transitional, other; plain), Legacy (driven: retained share of 2025 copper revenue), Latin America (Mexico, held for sale, ~1 quarter in 2027, nil in 2028; plain), Corporate (unallocated cost in corporate_ebit). Driven share of base revenue 86.2%, base residual 0.0%. Capex = cap_inv driver / revenue. EBIT is normalised GAAP (AT&T 'adjusted' definitions: excludes impairments, separation charges, acquired-intangible amortisation; SBC stays a cost), and D&A excludes acquired-intangible amortisation so EBITDA = AT&T adjusted EBITDA (FY2025 build 46,388 vs reported 46.4B). Value sits in three horizon multiples on NTM (Oct-2027 to Oct-2028) figures: EV/adj. EBITDA 6.2x (0.45), P/E 8.0x on a stated build EPS $2.88 (0.40) and FCF yield 12% on a stated build FCF to common $2.65/share (0.15). Minorities 17,985 (equity + redeemable NCI, mostly subsidiary preferred interests paying ~$1.5B/yr) and parent preferred 2,950 are treated as debt-like.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) My EBITDA path (+2.8%/+2.7% ex-Mexico in 2027/28) is below the company's 'improving to 5% or better in 2028' and my 2027 FCF ($17.2B) sits ~9% below the $19B+ guide that AT&T has never missed since 2023; I lean on wireless price competition under the SpaceX threat, fiber ARPU erosion and the Legacy drag, so this is the main variant. (2) The stated EPS and FCF/share are computed offline from the same driver build (scratch build2.py) and are not driver-linked in the engine; a driver change does not move them. (3) Equipment revenue is tied to subs at the FY2025 $310.6/sub, which understates 2026 equipment by ~$1.1B (near-zero margin, EBIT unaffected). (4) The ~$1.6B/yr pension/OPEB credit sits in other income: it is in EPS (P/E leg) but not in EBITDA, and the $8.1B postemployment obligation is not deducted. (5) Net debt at the horizon is stated (145,134) rather than bridged by the engine: 149,819 - Q4'26 FCF 6.0B - 0.75 x 2027 FCF 17.2B + dividends 7.3B + buybacks 7.75B + NCI distributions 1.5B - Mexico proceeds ~1.1B - Mexico held-for-sale leases 1.2B leaving. (6) Forged Fiber 37 (discontinued, held for sale, 50% JV with GIP/CPP) enters as a +4,080 x 0.9 adjustment at book; JV cash proceeds are undisclosed. fair_value.value equals the engine's base horizon value (23.09).
